newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts tip Adidas for DAX-30.
newsitem.headline: Analysts tip Adidas for DAX-30.

text.p: Sportswear manufacturer Adidas AG is likely to join the blue chip DAX when the 30-share index is reshuffled later this month, squeezing out retailer Karstadt AG, analysts said on Monday.

Adidas outranks Karstadt both in terms of market capitalisation and share turnover -- crucial criteria for membership of the index, according to separate reports by Commerzbank AG and by brokerage Independent Research.

Data already released by the Deutsche Boerse (German stock exchange) shows Adidas occupying the 27th position among German companies in terms of market capitalisation and the 29th place in terms of sales.
Karstadt, on the other hand, held the 34th place in sales and the 44th place in capitalisation.
One of the key criteria for the bourse's ruling on the DAX make-up is the so-called 35-35 rule, which says a DAX member must be among the top 35 in Germany both in terms of sales and capitalisation.

Deutsche Boerse will reach a decision on the DAX's structure at its regular summer index review on July 22. The announcement will be made in the late afternoon after the close of electronic share dealings.
Membership of the elite DAX is seen as a route to improved share liquidity and profile. Speculation that a company will join the index invariably boosts its share price.
The bourse will also take into account other considerations when deciding on the DAX, such as ensuring that an industry was adequately represented.
Independent Research said this would not be a problem in the case of Adidas since it belonged to the same sector as Karstadt.
In last year's DAX review, Deutsche Boerse ousted tyremaker Continental AG to admit Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG, the giant reinsurer which had long lobbied for a position.
The exchange also announced plans to later remove metals group Metallgesellschaft AG to make room for the giant Deutsche Telekom AG flotation in November.
